assumptions: Unknown regularity of the regression function
conclusion: A small prior scale can yield suboptimal contraction and overly optimistic uncertainty for rough truths, motivating adaptation of the scale to the data.
span: A smaller value of c cc corresponds to less variability in the prior process, and yields a posterior distribution with a less variable mean function and a smaller covariance. This is advantageous if the true regression function f ff is fairly regular, but will lead to a suboptimal contraction rate and a too optimistic quantification of remaining uncertainty in the opposite case (see [19, 16]). It is therefore important to adapt c cc to the data.
